newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Q2 interbank forex volume at record level.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Q2 interbank forex volume at record level.

text.p: The average daily volume of South Korea's overall foreign exchange transactions during the second quarter of this year was the largest ever at $2.31 billion, the central Bank of Korea said on Thursday.
This compared with $1.98 billion a year earlier.
A central bank statement attributed the sharp rise to stabilised won/dollar movement during the period, which boosted dealers' sentiment.
Dealers said they believed some interventions by the central bank in the market had slowed a fall in the local currency and caused the volume increase.
The statement said $66.36 million flowed into the interbank foreign exchange market from April to June, while dollar demand reached $62.82 billion.
Improving exports and foreign funds for equity investment in the local stock market contributed to the rising dollar supply during the period.
South Korea raised the foreign stock holding limit to 23 percent on May 2 from the previous 20 percent.
The statement said the daily average of spot transactions reached $2.23 billion in the three-month period against $1.96 billion a year earlier.
That of forward transactions rose to $76 million, compared with $21 million.
The spot transactions market comprised 96.7 percent of all foreign exchange trading during the second quarter, compared to 98.9 percent a year ago.
Domestic banks accounted for 66.5 percent of overall foreign exchange transactions in the three-month period, while foreign banks operating in Korea took the rest.
The statement said South Korea's won appreciated by 1.0 percent to 888.10 won at the end of the second quarter from 897.10 at the end of the first quarter.
The won weakened to 775.29 won per 100 yen at the end of the second quarter from 723.18 won at the end of the first quarter.
Sterling also strengthened to 1,478.46 won at the end of the second quarter against 1,463.17.
